title: Boss: a week on the team
summary: Rejected pushes, a stale force push, a fork and a release: handle each the way a senior engineer would, and build the release tooling.

steps.title: The scene
steps.body: Monday to Friday on a five-person team: you get rejected by the server, review a teammate's PR, contribute a fix to an open-source dependency through a fork, and cut Friday's release. The questions are the decisions; the code is the tooling your team runs in CI.

steps.prompt: Monday: `git push` is rejected (*fetch first*). You have 2 local commits, nothing pushed. The team wants linear history. What do you run?
steps.explain: Replay your unpushed commits on top of the teammate's work. Force would delete their commits; `reset --hard` would delete yours.

steps.prompt: Wednesday: you squashed your PR branch and ran `git push --force-with-lease`. It says *stale info*. Your reviewer mentioned they pushed a small fix to your branch. What next?
options: `git fetch`, cherry-pick or rebase their commit into your branch, then `git push --force-with-lease` again
Switch to `git push --force` so it goes through
Delete the remote branch and push again
Ignore it; the lease is advisory
steps.explain: The lease just saved the reviewer's commit. Bring it in, then push.

steps.title: Release notes
prompt: Friday's release job groups the commits since the last tag. Write `Notes(List<string> subjects)` returning the release notes text:
- `feat...: text` goes under `## Features`, `fix...: text` under `## Fixes`, in the order given; the bullet is the text after the first `: `.
- Other types are left out. Omit a heading whose section is empty.
hints: `s[(s.IndexOf(": ") + 2)..]` is the text after the type.
Build a `List<string>` of lines and join at the end.
template:
Dojo.Eq("both sections", "## Features
- add gift cards
## Fixes
- handle empty cart
- round VAT per line",
Notes(new() { "fix: handle empty cart", "docs: readme", "feat: add gift cards", "fix(tax): round VAT per line" }));
Dojo.Eq("fixes only", "## Fixes\n- one", Notes(new() { "fix: one", "chore: deps" }));

steps.title: Can I push?
prompt: Before pushing, a helper script tells you what to do. Write `Advice(string local, string remote, parents, bool branchIsShared)` combining your earlier models:
- `"pull"` if `local` is an ancestor of `remote` (you are behind);
- diverged: `"pull --rebase, then push"` if `branchIsShared`, otherwise `"push --force-with-lease"` (it is your own branch, which you rewrote).
starter: static string Advice(string local, string remote, Dictionary<string, string[]> parents, bool branchIsShared)
solution: static HashSet<string> Ancestors(string start, Dictionary<string, string[]> parents)
static string Advice(string local, string remote, Dictionary<string, string[]> parents, bool branchIsShared)
hints: Two ancestor checks, then the diverged case.
Equality first, or both checks would be true.
template: Dojo.Eq("same", "nothing to push", Advice("C", "C", dojoG, true));
Dojo.Eq("diverged shared branch", "pull --rebase, then push", Advice("C", "E", dojoG, true));
Dojo.Eq("diverged own rewritten branch", "push --force-with-lease", Advice("C", "E", dojoG, false));

steps.title: Tag the release
prompt: Combine versioning and notes. Write `Release(string lastTag, List<string> subjects)` returning:
- otherwise two lines: `git tag -a <next> -m "Release <next without v>"` then `git push origin <next>`.
starter: static string Release(string lastTag, List<string> subjects)
solution: static string NextVersion(string current, List<string> subjects)
int major = parts[0], minor = parts[1], patch = parts[2];
bool breaking = subjects.Any(s => s.Contains("BREAKING CHANGE") || s.Split(':')[0].EndsWith("!"));
static string Release(string lastTag, List<string> subjects)
hints: Escape the quotes inside the interpolated string: `\"`.
template: Dojo.Eq("minor release", "git tag -a v1.5.0 -m \"Release 1.5.0\"\ngit push origin v1.5.0", Release("v1.4.2", new() { "feat: gift cards" }));
Dojo.Eq("nothing releasable", "no release", Release("v1.4.2", new() { "chore: tidy" }));
